Formlabs uses a proprietary resin cartridge... it's the paper printers situation all over again, the printers themselves are not that expensive but the disposable ink costs an arm and a leg.

Don't go with Formlabs, support any of the open-platform alternatives.

And also, be aware that these printers require some serious development work (you need solvent to wash away uncured resin (if you ask me, this basically necessitates a chemical hood... Formlabs will happily upsell the "Form Wash" for this for another 699). If uncured resin falls on your floor (which has happened to me a little too many times), boy is it a horror cleaning it up even if you have industrial grade solvents; FDM printers are easier and their "ink" is much, much less expensive by comparison.

I don't care what they say. Having done resin printing, it's toxic and fiddly and you can very very easily ruin your machine. The auxiliary chemicals like isopropyl alcohol are toxic as well, and need to be changed quite regularly if you want to avoid your prints getting an oily sheen.

It also generates copious amount of hazardous waste. Anything that has to do with this degree of material safety hazards should not be a hobby.

Before resin printing, lots of people had a hobby doing resin casts, the forums are full of health-related horror stories, this thing can and will kill you over time.

I have a resin printer (elegoo mars 2p) and have done a number of small "production" runs of things that don't really matter.

I have to say that it is the biggest pain in the arse thing I even own. While the prints come out "good", I find that dimensional accuracy is often really not good at all; and that the whole rinse in isopropyl, finish in the sun process is just a sticky, irritating, and probably carcinogenic drag.

And I can't imagine why USD700 is regarded as a bargain.

So this has served as a fine reminder - I need to sell this damn thing, it just takes up space.

This thing is all over YouTube, they really backed up the truck to the Influencer Club and started handing out the goods. Lots of people I like and respect have showcased it, like Applied Science, Jeff Geerling, among others.

But although there's a lot of discussion about how large a discount this is from FormLab's 8 billion dollar printers, there is absolutely NO comparison that I can find to other brands! OK, it's a cheaper Bentley - but how does it compare to the Toyota or Honda that we can get down the street? There are loads of options with --on paper-- better specs for half this price or less.

You don't want a resin printer. They are nasty, chemically, they require you to set up a "hot zone", you need ppe, venting is really important. When your print works good, you still have to wash it and then cure it. Changing colors ids like a whole event.

FDM printers are amazing now. Strongly recommend an FDM printer.

For instance, I wanted to buy a smart device to control my mini-split and it was 160$ on amazon for 1. Well I built 5 for 80$ in a weekend (excluding the 7 days shipping from China).

I'm very much looking for someone convince me not to buy this? Seems like people don't enjoy resin because it's a tad messy and it has a ~10-30 curing process.

Yet all parts from my FDM printer feels cheap and looks like nothing I'd be happy to buy unless I spend HOURS sanding and painting.

Resin printing has its place but it's terribly messy and the FDM printers are getting so good these days it's basically trivial to print even complex multi part prints.

I'm in the market for a new resin printer (I have a bunch of old ones) and no idea why I would buy this/why this is an improvement off my current printer based on what is presented on the marketing pages. Pass. I didn't buy the prusa resin printer but at least they were really good at communicating what the actual value was for folk who already have resin printers. This just seems like it's aimed at SLA novices

My anycube costs a fraction of this and I don't need to shell out for any proprietary nonsense like cartridges. I use all open source tooling as well. For $700 I got a resin printer, several diverse resin types, a fume extraction hood/enclosure, a infrared curing box and automatic washer tank.

I used to use an older, more expensive version from FormLabs in my last company to print our (more accurate) version of Invisalign negatives, and we'd thermoform the aligners over the top of the cured resin (with a barrier).

The accuracy was great. They'd hold up. Printing took a while, but generally pretty solid as we scaled from in-house to full lab setup. They're great as resin printers go.
